case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Attributable student authorship and transparent, authorised AI assessment assistance.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: Operative instruments (N002, N136, N141, N001) supported by N133 require the final submission to be the student's own work, prohibit unapproved or undisclosed GenAI use, and provide authenticity monitoring and appeal remedies.
case_summary.case_note: Curtin prescribes that GenAI use in assessment requires explicit Unit Coordinator permission and transparent disclosure, and that the final submission must be the student's own work (N002, N133, N136, N141). All S1 critical-risk safeguards—attributable authorship, disclosure, human accountability, equity, and appeal remedies—are addressed (D5=3, Critical gap=No), though Unit Coordinator permission criteria and steps remain undocumented (D2=2, D4=2). Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Prevention or enforceable refusal of unverified AI-produced assessment being claimed as the student's own.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: Under Protocol v1.1, an enforceable prohibition protects the critical risk: Curtin prohibits submitting AI-generated output as one's own work (N136, N133), requires authenticity verification and Confirmation Checks (N002), and enforces penalties under N141.
case_summary.case_note: Curtin prohibits students from submitting AI-drafted work as their own without explicit permission and disclosure, treating unapproved or undisclosed GenAI output as academic misconduct (N136, N133, N141). Operative assessment rules also require staff authenticity verification, Confirmation Checks, and 50% Secure Assessment or monitoring (N002), so S2's critical risk is protected (D5=3, Critical gap=No). Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15.

case_summary.case_note: Curtin restricts ICT assets to authorised purposes (N005), requires human oversight for AI (N001), mandates student-authored assessment verified by authenticity checks (N002), and prohibits impersonation and unfair academic conduct (N136, N141). Critical gap is Uncertain because N005 (effective August/September 2026) superseded N153 and moved operational account-use rules to the unavailable ICT Appropriate Use Procedures. Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15.

documents_checked.document_title: Copyright and GenAI teaching accessibility and protected material
documents_checked.text:
Anyone who has a disability can use copyrighted material with Gen-AI or AI powered tools for
accessibility purposes to support personal study and learning. This includes using
Curtin-owned teaching and learning material (such as lecture slides, lecture recordings,
captions or transcripts). Curtin staff can also use this provision to assist students who have
accessibility needs. Ensure that:
Gen-AI tools used are secure (e.g. they do not train on or share content)
Outputs are not shared publicly (e.g. posted on the open internet)

Principle 6: Transparency, Explainability and Contestability
Develop, deploy and use AI systems in a way that maximises transparency,
explainability and contestability. Allow stakeholders to know when AI has
been used and contest decisions made using AI.

case_summary.case_note: Curtin requires AI transparency and privacy compliance (N001), restricts uploading lecture slides or audio transcripts to GenAI tools except for disability accessibility (N133, N231), and regulates University data collection via consent (N016, N017). documents_checked.text:
If your clash is between a lecture and another class activity, you may choose not to register for
the lecture and instead watch the recording via iLecture, as long as recordings are available
and there are no attendance requirements, assessments or other compulsory activities
scheduled during the lecture time; you may need to wait until the unit outline is published in
OASIS (approximately one week before teaching starts) to confirm.

2.2 Verification of identity and authority
Before any personal information is disclosed, staff receiving any request for the release of
personal information will:
(a) undertake a verification process with the requestor and assure themselves of the
requestor’s identity. This will be done at the discretion of the staff member to a
reasonable level and may be completed by sighting and confirming identifying
information; and
(b) where the request is made by a third party (that is, by someone who is not the person
who owns the personal information), obtain evidence of the requestor’s authority to
seek information, unless otherwise authorised pursuant to these procedures.

case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: N002 s.2.8.1 requires group submissions to declare each member's responsibilities, N136/N133 prohibit unapproved or undisclosed GenAI use, N001 Principle 3 requires equity/inclusion, and discretionary general-purpose AI use does not block participation without an alternative.
case_summary.case_note: Curtin requires group work submissions to declare which members are responsible for which portions (N002 s.2.8.1), prohibits unapproved or undisclosed GenAI use (N133, N136, N141), and upholds equity and inclusion in AI (N001). Because discretionary general-purpose AI use does not block participation and attribution/disclosure rules are operative, S7's critical risk is protected (D5=3, Critical gap=No). Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Authorised AI assessment contributions, accountable human group responsibility and protection of group personal information.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: While N002 s.2.8.1 and N136/N133 govern human group responsibility and GenAI permission, no operative policy governs persistent AI agents joining student group workspaces with cross-session memory or protects group personal information in student-managed digital workspaces.
case_summary.case_note: Curtin requires group contribution declarations (N002 s.2.8.1), GenAI permission and disclosure (N133, N136), and privacy/security compliance (N001, N017). However, no operative rule governs persistent AI agents joining student group workspaces with cross-session memory or protects group personal information in student-selected workspaces (D5=2, Critical gap=Yes). Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15.

documents_checked.text:
Principle 6: Transparency, Explainability and Contestability
Develop, deploy and use AI systems in a way that maximises transparency,
explainability and contestability. Allow stakeholders to know when AI has
been used and contest decisions made using AI.
Principle 7: Accountability
Implement human oversight, review and the ability to intervene for all AI-
based functions and decisions. Identify the individual accountable for any
decision made using AI. Maintain records on the use of AI to comply with
recordkeeping obligations.

case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: N002 PC2 s.2.4 prohibits unverified AI grading by restricting AI grading/feedback to approved staff pilots with mandatory staff output verification and human marking on appeal, reinforced by N002 s.2.8 and N001 Principles 6-7.
case_summary.case_note: Curtin's N002 PC2 s.2.4 restricts GenAI grading or feedback to staff pilots approved by the Dean (Learning and Teaching), Privacy Officer, and CIO/CISO, requiring staff verification of all outputs, advance student declaration, and human marking on appeal. Combined with fair group mark allocation (N002 s.2.8) and AI accountability and contestability (N001), unreviewed AI evaluations cannot determine binding marks (D5=3, Critical gap=No). Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15.

documents_checked.document_title: Curtin University AI Use in Research
documents_checked.text:
AI tools can enhance research by quickly summarising or refining text, analysing large data sets, crafting and debugging code, communicating research
results and streamlining repetitive tasks. To use them well, researchers need to protect intellectual integrity and authorship, safeguard intellectual
property (including Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property), use data in culturally appropriate ways, and keep human oversight and expert
judgement at the centre of their work. AI tools must never substitute for human critical thinking, expertise and evaluation.
The guidelines apply to all Curtin researchers, including research students in master and doctoral programs. They cover generative AI tools for text,
images, audio, code and data, as well as generative AI-driven support platforms. They should be read alongside Curtin’s Artificial Intelligence Policy and
the policies of publishers, funders and governments relevant to your research.

documents_checked.document_title: Curtin University AI Use in Research
documents_checked.text:
AI tools can enhance research by quickly summarising or refining text, analysing large data sets, crafting and debugging code, communicating research
results and streamlining repetitive tasks. To use them well, researchers need to protect intellectual integrity and authorship, safeguard intellectual
property (including Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property), use data in culturally appropriate ways, and keep human oversight and expert
judgement at the centre of their work. AI tools must never substitute for human critical thinking, expertise and evaluation.
The guidelines apply to all Curtin researchers, including research students in master and doctoral programs. They cover generative AI tools for text,
images, audio, code and data, as well as generative AI-driven support platforms. They should be read alongside Curtin’s Artificial Intelligence Policy and
the policies of publishers, funders and governments relevant to your research.

documents_checked.document_title: Curtin University AI Use in Research
documents_checked.text:
AI tools can enhance research by quickly summarising or refining text, analysing large data sets, crafting and debugging code, communicating research
results and streamlining repetitive tasks. To use them well, researchers need to protect intellectual integrity and authorship, safeguard intellectual
property (including Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property), use data in culturally appropriate ways, and keep human oversight and expert
judgement at the centre of their work. AI tools must never substitute for human critical thinking, expertise and evaluation.
The guidelines apply to all Curtin researchers, including research students in master and doctoral programs. They cover generative AI tools for text,
images, audio, code and data, as well as generative AI-driven support platforms. They should be read alongside Curtin’s Artificial Intelligence Policy and
the policies of publishers, funders and governments relevant to your research.

15. Right of appeal
15.1 A Student may appeal a decision of the Authorised Oﬃcer or Student Conduct Panel that Student
Misconduct has occurred and/or any Penalty imposed:
(a) within 7 days of a decision made or Penalty imposed under the Pathway 1 Process; or
(b) within 14 days of a decision made or Penalty imposed under the Pathway 2 Process.
15.2 In exceptional circumstances, the Academic Registrar may give a Student more time to appeal.

and monitor their performance. Adopt safety measures proportionate to the
magnitude of potential risks.
Principle 6: Transparency, Explainability and Contestability
Develop, deploy and use AI systems in a way that maximises transparency,
explainability and contestability. Allow stakeholders to know when AI has
been used and contest decisions made using AI.
Principle 7: Accountability
Implement human oversight, review and the ability to intervene for all AI-
based functions and decisions. Identify the individual accountable for any
decision made using AI. Maintain records on the use of AI to comply with
recordkeeping obligations.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Informed, purpose-limited collection and lawful course-end memory restriction/disposal, with access and security protections.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: While N150 PC12, N011, N016/N017, and N001 require consent, minimisation, security, and avoiding retention beyond minimum periods, the external Retention and Disposal Authorities (WAUSDA), Disposal of Information guide (N011 s.3.8), and N001 s.6 AI procedures are absent from the bundle and could establish lawful course-end disposal (No) or leave it unaddressed (Yes).
case_summary.case_note: Curtin prescribes overlapping general frameworks (N001, N150 PC12, N010/N011, N016/N017, N005/N006) requiring prior consent, minimisation, security, and disposal when retention periods end. Critical gap is Uncertain because WAUSDA/Retention and Disposal Authorities, the Disposal of Information guide (N011 s.3.8), and N001 Section 6 AI procedures are unavailable in the bundle. Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15.

Develop, deploy and use AI systems in a way that maximises transparency,
explainability and contestability. Allow stakeholders to know when AI has
been used and contest decisions made using AI.
Principle 7: Accountability
Implement human oversight, review and the ability to intervene for all AI-
based functions and decisions. Identify the individual accountable for any
decision made using AI. Maintain records on the use of AI to comply with
recordkeeping obligations.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Informed purpose and cross-course use, accountable lifecycle ownership, access/correction and contestability of consequential profiling.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: Although N150 PC12, N016, N017, and N001 provide general consent, data-update, FOI access/correction, and contestability principles, Curtin lacks an operational rule assigning accountable lifecycle ownership for cross-course AI learner profiling, ensuring unit instructors know of its cross-course scope, and governing contestability of consequential profiling.
case_summary.case_note: Curtin's N150 PC12, N016/N017, and N001 provide prior consent, secondary-use PIA controls, FOI access and correction, and AI transparency and contestability principles. However, no operative rule assigns accountable lifecycle ownership for persistent cross-course AI learner profiling, informs instructors of cross-course profile scope, or operationalises contestability of consequential profiling (D5=2, Critical gap=Yes). Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Purpose-bounded authorisation for combined standing powers, with security, intervention and contestability of consequential actions.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: Curtin's governance is siloed across separate instruments (N001, N005/N006, N007, N011, N002) with no connected purpose-bounded authorisation, cross-system ownership, or operational intervention and contestability workflow for an AI agent exercising standing authority across LMS, student support, enrolment, advising, and assessment systems without per-action human review.
case_summary.case_note: Curtin mandates human oversight, intervention, and contestability for AI (N001), restricts ICT assets to authorised purposes (N005/N006), and assigns system-level access controls (N011). However, institutional ownership and oversight remain siloed across separate policies without purpose-bounded authorisation or connected intervention/contestability for an agent with standing powers across LMS, enrolment, advising, support, and assessment (D5=2, Critical gap=Yes). Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15.
